narrative.summary: Engine complaints dominate owner reports for this model year, with owners describing oil leaks discovered during ordinary driving and parking situations, in some cases escalating to fires or crashes. Visibility and wiper complaints form the next largest cluster, with owners reporting intermittent instrument cluster warning behavior while driving in reverse. Electrical system and powertrain complaints round out the picture, with owners describing unexplained warning chimes and sudden, complete loss of drive power.

narrative.summary: Electrical system faults are the most-reported problem category, with owners describing battery failures that caused physical damage to nearby components. Steering complaints frequently involve loss of vehicle control during cornering, while a notable share of reports describe the StabiliTrak stability-control system triggering autonomously and reducing engine power without driver input. Brake-related complaints overlap with the steering and stability-control accounts, appearing in loss-of-control incidents on slippery roads.

Engine stalls and check-engine warnings, as well as stability control and traction-control alerts accompanied by vibration and unintended braking, round out the primary complaint picture.

narrative.summary: Exterior lighting problems make up the largest share of owner complaints, with rear lighting described as dangerously bright to following drivers. Seat ventilation malfunctions and electrical system issues — sometimes tied to acceleration hesitation — round out the most frequently reported concerns. A smaller portion of reports involve the engine, with some complaints in both the electrical and engine categories noting fires or crashes.

narrative.headline: What 2014 Honda Accord owners report most
narrative.summary: Electrical system complaints make up the largest share of owner reports, with several owners describing sudden, unintended vehicle movement at low speeds without driver input. Engine and steering complaints follow, with owners noting intermittent hesitation under acceleration and handling difficulties in cold weather. Brake-related reports frequently describe loss of power steering assist accompanied by a dashboard warning light, suggesting an overlap between the steering and electrical concerns.

Tire-related reports echo the sensor warning theme, with the indicator illuminating during normal highway driving.

narrative.headline: What 2015 Chevrolet Tahoe owners report most
narrative.summary: Service brake complaints make up the largest share of owner reports, with drivers describing a warning message appearing on the dash and the brake pedal requiring unusual force to slow the vehicle. Electrical system faults are the second most common area, covering failures of the audio system and the loss of audible safety chimes. Steering and powertrain complaints round out the top concerns, with owners reporting the vehicle unexpectedly engaging four-wheel drive, causing difficulty steering and sudden jerking.

A smaller share of reports concerns airbags failing to deploy in side-impact collisions.

narrative.headline: What 2015 Ford Focus owners report most
narrative.summary: The dominant pattern in owner complaints is sudden, unexpected loss of drive power, most often reported during low-speed maneuvers such as pulling away from a stop. A dashboard warning indicator — described as a wrench icon with a service message — commonly accompanies these power-loss events, and owners note that the situation creates a safety exposure when traffic is present. Steering and fuel/propulsion complaints round out the picture, with some incidents involving crashes or fires.

narrative.summary: Engine complaints make up the largest share of owner reports, with the most common pattern being sudden, complete loss of power while driving — the car shuts off mid-highway, the dashboard goes dark, and the accelerator stops responding. Service brake complaints round out the top concerns, with some incidents also involving fires or crashes.

narrative.headline: What 2015 Jeep Grand Cherokee owners report most
narrative.summary: The dominant pattern across owner complaints centers on powertrain behavior, particularly harsh or unexpected transmission shifts that dealers often dismiss as normal. A notable share of owners also report the gear shifter moving on its own while the vehicle is in motion, and a smaller but concerning cluster describes electrical anomalies — erratic wipers, radio cutouts, and jerking hesitation — sometimes preceding more serious incidents. Fires and crashes appear across the powertrain, engine, and electrical categories.

narrative.headline: What 2016 Ford Explorer owners report most
narrative.summary: Structure-related complaints make up the largest share of owner reports, with steering failures and engine noise also appearing frequently across the complaint set. Exterior lighting draws the second-largest share of complaints, centered on low-beam headlights that owners describe as failing to adequately illuminate the road ahead. Engine and fuel/propulsion reports are less frequent but include accounts of fire and cabin intrusion of irritating compounds.

narrative.headline: What 2016 Jeep Cherokee owners report most
narrative.summary: The dominant pattern in owner complaints is powertrain trouble, particularly the transmission shutting down unexpectedly while the vehicle is in motion. Engine stalling without warning — sometimes requiring multiple restart attempts — and electrical system failures that leave the vehicle unable to restart are also widely reported. Brake-related complaints, which include software upgrades noted by dealers, round out the picture of a vehicle whose owners frequently report losing control of basic driving functions.

Fuel and propulsion complaints mirror the powertrain pattern, with repeated hesitation on take-off reported even on low-mileage vehicles fresh from the dealership.

Powertrain communication issues — where the vehicle behaves as though it has slipped into neutral after the accelerator is released — also appear across reports.

narrative.headline: What 2017 Honda Accord owners report most
narrative.summary: Electrical system faults are the most commonly reported problem, with owners describing unexpected behavior from vehicle controls while the car is parked and unoccupied. Engine and fuel/propulsion complaints follow, including reports of stalling, fire risk, and a widely noted lag in throttle response when accelerating from a stop. Service brake reports center on the collision-detection system triggering unintended hard braking in active traffic.

narrative.headline: What 2017 Hyundai Tucson owners report most
narrative.summary: The dominant pattern across owner complaints is sudden hesitation or complete lack of response when pressing the accelerator — most often when pulling away from a stop, merging, turning at intersections, or resuming speed in stop-and-go traffic. A substantial share of reports also describe the transmission failing to shift through gears in the expected sequence, sometimes dropping into a neutral-like state under acceleration. Electrical system complaints follow a similar hesitation pattern tied to the dual-clutch transmission, with some owners noting the same behavior was reported for the prior model year.

narrative.summary: Powertrain complaints dominate owner reports for this model, with transmission behavior being the most common concern. Electrical system failures, including unexpected shutdowns while driving, make up the next largest share of complaints, with some incidents involving fires or crashes. Engine and speed control issues round out the picture, with owners describing stop/start system interruptions and unintended acceleration during cruise control use.

narrative.headline: 2018 Chevy Tahoe: brakes lead owner complaints and carry the most serious risk

Service brakes are the top concern at 20% of reports, and they are also the only area tied to serious harm here: 2 crashes, 1 injury, and 1 death. Engine and power train issues follow closely at 19% and 18%, then electrical at 13% and steering at 12%. No fires were reported in any category.

A secondary cluster of complaints describes the powertrain and steering losing function progressively — warning systems dropping out, speed becoming restricted, and power steering disappearing — often in vehicles with very low accumulated mileage. Some incidents across multiple component areas involved fires or crashes.

Engine stalling events also appear in the data, sometimes attributed to fuel delivery components.

narrative.headline: Engine and transmission complaints dominate the 2018 Ford Fusion
narrative.summary: Of 422 owner complaints filed with NHTSA, engine problems are by far the most common, accounting for 193 reports (46%). The transmission/drivetrain is the next biggest concern at 103 reports (24%), followed by engine cooling at 86 (20%). Most reports describe no crash or fire, but the electrical system shows 1 fire and 1 crash, and the power train has 1 crash. Buyers should focus their inspection on the engine and transmission.

narrative.headline: 2018 Ford Mustang: engine and drivetrain dominate owner complaints
narrative.summary: Owners filed 182 complaints with NHTSA. Engine problems lead by far at 53 reports (29%), followed by power train at 43 (24%) and electrical at 30 (16%) — together more than two-thirds of all complaints. Most reports are non-injury, but the data does include one fire and one crash tied to the engine, four crashes tied to the power train, and one fire and one injury tied to the electrical system. Smaller clusters cover the convertible structure and door latches. The takeaway: focus a test drive and inspection on how the engine and drivetrain behave.

narrative.headline: 2018 Subaru Outback: electrical and mirror complaints lead the list
narrative.summary: Electrical system faults make up the largest share of owner complaints, with the key fob losing function after the vehicle is locked while hazard lights are active being the most-described pattern. Visibility and wiper issues form the second-largest cluster, driven primarily by complaints that the driver-side exterior mirror cannot be adjusted far enough to eliminate blind spots. A smaller number of owners also report unexpected engine stalls and shutoffs while driving, and a separate set of visibility complaints echoes the mirror-adjustment limitation from a different angle.

narrative.headline: 2018 Toyota Camry: power train leads the owner complaints
narrative.summary: Power train and braking concerns dominate owner complaints for this generation Camry, with throttle response and transmission behavior appearing across multiple component categories. Owners consistently describe a hesitation or lag when accelerating from low speeds, where the vehicle is slow to respond even under firm pedal input. Brake-related complaints include reported malfunctions and failures of brake assist systems, in some cases tied to crashes.

narrative.headline: Air bags are the biggest concern, and the most serious one to check
narrative.summary: Across 133 owner complaints filed with NHTSA, air bags are by far the most reported area, with 35 reports (26%) tied to 16 crashes, 12 injuries, 1 fire, and 1 death. The next four areas are all fuel- and engine-related: the fuel/propulsion system drew 23 reports (17%) with 1 fire and 1 injury, while the fuel system, gasoline, and engine each drew 15 reports (11%) with 1 fire apiece. If you are looking at one of these cars, air bag deployment is the issue to take most seriously.

A secondary cluster of complaints involves the engine and electrical system, where owners describe sudden and complete vehicle shutdown — including loss of hazard lights — attributed to a ground wire separating from the ECM while the vehicle was in motion or stopped at a light. A smaller share of owners also report the vehicle running roughly and stalling without warning at moderate speeds.

narrative.summary: Electrical and advanced driver-assistance system failures dominate owner complaints for this model, with dashboard warning lights activating unexpectedly and collision-mitigation and lane-keeping systems dropping out while the vehicle is in motion. Forward collision avoidance and lane departure systems generate overlapping reports, often describing the same warning message appearing on the dashboard, suggesting the issues may be related. Engine-area complaints round out the top concerns, with at least some reports describing seat hardware behavior that owners characterize as a safety issue.

narrative.headline: 2019 Jeep Cherokee: the transmission tops owner complaints
narrative.summary: The most-reported problems center on the power train, where owners describe sluggish or dangerously delayed downshifts during highway and city driving. Engine stalls — occurring both while stationary and at speed — make up a large share of the remaining complaints, and electrical faults affecting the infotainment screen and running lights are also widely reported. A smaller number of owners report engine failures and unexpected shutdowns linked under the steering category.

Fires show up across most categories, so treat any burning smell, warning light, or hesitation seriously.

narrative.headline: 2019 Ram 1500: electrical and steering top the complaint list
narrative.summary: Electrical system faults make up the largest share of owner complaints, with steering failures close behind — both categories include reports of fires and crashes. Owners most commonly describe sudden loss of vehicle control or unexpected behavior immediately after taking delivery, sometimes within days of purchase. Engine and powertrain complaints frequently overlap, with reports of unintended acceleration accompanied by multiple warning lights illuminating at once.

narrative.summary: The most-reported concern among owners involves the forward collision avoidance system, where the automatic emergency braking activates unexpectedly without a clear obstacle. Electrical system failures — including complete loss of motor power and the inability to shift into neutral — make up the next most-common category, sometimes accompanied by fires or crashes. Air bag and suspension complaints round out the top problem areas, with owners describing screen blackouts and, in the most serious cases, complete wheel and suspension separation.

narrative.headline: 2019 Toyota Camry: powertrain and transmission gripes lead the complaints
narrative.summary: Of 378 owner complaints filed with NHTSA, the top three areas are all drivetrain-related: Power Train (106 reports, 28%), Engine (77, 20%), and Fuel/Propulsion System (63, 17%). Most are about how the car shifts and accelerates, with no fires reported. The safety-flagged complaints concentrate in Service Brakes, where 5 owners reported a crash and 4 reported injuries.

narrative.summary: The dominant pattern in owner complaints centers on propulsion and engine behavior, with many owners reporting that the vehicle fails to accelerate when the accelerator pedal is pressed, particularly when pulling away from stops. Electrical system glitches and structural issues — including dashboard reflections interfering with mirror visibility — make up a meaningful share of the remaining reports. Complaints across several areas note incidents involving fires or crashes, indicating that some reported symptoms occurred in high-stakes driving situations.

narrative.headline: 2019 Toyota Sienna: drivetrain and acceleration top the complaint list
narrative.summary: Owners filed 45 complaints with NHTSA. The two biggest clusters are tied: power train problems and fuel/propulsion (acceleration) issues, at 7 reports (16%) each. Body/structure follows with 6 reports (13%), including the only injury in the data. Another 6 reports (13%) each cite the fuel system and gasoline, largely tied to a recall. No fires, crashes, or deaths were reported across these complaints.

narrative.headline: 2019 Toyota Tacoma: brakes and fuel system top the owner complaints
narrative.summary: Owners filed 209 complaints with NHTSA. The two biggest clusters are the fuel/propulsion system (55 reports, 26%) and the service brakes (51 reports, 24%). Brakes are the most safety-relevant group, tied to 5 crashes and 2 injuries. Power train (40) and engine (27) issues follow, and the engine and electrical groups each include a reported fire. Worth a careful test drive and inspection of these areas before buying.

Electrical failures stand out because they appear to cascade — owners report losing power steering and brake effectiveness in the same event as the shutoff. Engine complaints also appear at a similar rate, with some reports mentioning transmission grinding alongside unrelated trim and latch concerns.

narrative.headline: Power train complaints lead the 2020 Chevrolet Camaro
narrative.summary: From 31 owner reports to NHTSA, power train problems are the most common, named in 32% of complaints, followed by electrical issues at 19%. Engine and vehicle speed control each account for 13%, and exterior lighting rounds out the list at 6%. Most reports describe reliability problems, but a few turned dangerous: 3 power-train complaints and 1 speed-control complaint involved a crash, and 1 injury was reported. No fires or deaths were reported. The details below are worth a read.

narrative.headline: 2020 Chevrolet Colorado: power train tops owner complaints
narrative.summary: Across 79 owner complaints to NHTSA, power train problems lead by a wide margin at 32 reports (41%), more than double any other area. Engine (14, 18%), steering (9, 11%), service brakes (8, 10%), and electrical system (6, 8%) follow. None of these reports involved a crash and there were no deaths, but service brakes account for 2 fires and 3 injuries, and engine and electrical each include 1 fire.

The next-largest cluster is the power train (45 reports, 19%). Together, engine and power train make up over 60% of all complaints, so power-loss and stalling are the main things to watch. Smaller but real flags: steering shows up in fewer reports (19, 8%) yet carries the most crashes (5) and 2 injuries, and headlight/exterior-lighting visibility comes up in 27 reports (11%).

narrative.headline: Power train complaints dominate the 2020 Jeep Cherokee, with a few engine fires reported
narrative.summary: Of 248 owner complaints filed with NHTSA, power train problems are the most common by far at 132 reports (53%), more than half of all complaints. The engine is the next biggest concern at 35 reports (14%), and notably accounts for 5 fires. The electrical system follows at 33 reports (13%), with no fires, crashes, or injuries reported. Service brakes and steering round out the top issues, together involving 3 crashes and 1 injury. Buyers should test-drive carefully for stalling and shifting problems and have the engine inspected before buying.

narrative.headline: 2020 Toyota Corolla: engine and drivetrain complaints lead, brakes and airbags carry the most risk
narrative.summary: Owners filed 301 complaints to NHTSA. By far the biggest theme is the engine, named in 36% of reports, with the powertrain adding another 11% — together nearly half of all complaints point at how the car drives and shifts. The next areas are the electrical system (10%), service brakes (7%), and airbags (6%). The two smaller categories are the ones to take most seriously: brakes appear in 6 crashes, and airbags in 9 crashes with 12 people injured.

Service brake complaints describe unexpected brake engagement accompanied by unusual sounds while driving downhill.

Secondary clusters cover the braking and speed control systems — specifically the removal of a low regenerative braking option that owners expected from their test drives — and electrical system faults that cause climate control heating to stop working.

Engine is the most reported area at 33%, followed by air bags and power train (17% each), then tires and the fuel/propulsion system (8% each). Almost all reports are about reliability rather than safety; the one exception is an air bag complaint tied to a crash. No fires, injuries, or deaths were reported in any category.
